items.title: 67559_Art Hodes oral history interview
items.q: Scobie says, all right, how would you like to have your own band opposite me, a quartet? I says, fine, whatever money is fine. So I got Nappy Trotter, Buddy Smith, Earl Murphy, Art Hodes.

ctx.x: if I go with him, then I no longer can decide my fate. I might not come back to Chicago for two years, and what am I going to do with my family? I got kids and everything. I can't do it.

So Scobie I couldn't do it, either. Scobie says, all right, how would you like to have your own band opposite me, a quartet? I says, fine, whatever money is fine. So I got Nappy Trotter, Buddy Smith, Earl Murphy, Art Hodes. Fine, great. Now, Nappy immediately gets a complex. He's got to go on after Scobie, in the band. So go out to the bar and get ready to play and all that, and got a show on.

Now, it was the easiest job in the world. All we had to do was play that intermission. Now, instead of letting it down so that the people could -- they had an hour and a quarter show. They were raised to the sky, here we come, the thundering herd. Like man, you know, to break it down. Buddy Smith is not going to be backstaged by Dave Black. It was a scene, you know? And Bob Scobie had meanwhile taken me aside and said, Art, can't you talk to those guys? It's not that -- I'm not worried about them cutting us or…
